content.text:
Joaquin, the project's description went to the wrong place. The opening paragraph ("A foundation model for tree/loop scattering amplitudes…", the research threads) was filed under the model section. That section is pushed only when an agent touches the model code: `models/`, `wrappers.py`, `particle_ids.py`, `config/model/`. An agent working on data, generation or an analysis would never see what the project is.

**Why that happened.** My test sorted every passage into a rule or reference for one kind of work. A project description is neither: it's orientation that every task needs, because it's what lets an agent judge why it's doing anything. The test had no slot for that, so the description fell into the nearest topic.

**When the sections are fed, as drafted.** The first time an agent reads or edits a matching file, or runs a matching command, that section is injected into its context, once per agent. Reads are caught after the call, and acting commands like submissions, sweep generators and git merges before it, so the agent has the section before it acts.

**Why not feed everything always:**
1. **Cost.** Everything in CLAUDE.md is re-read on every call of every agent. At about 30k tokens, that was 99M tokens yesterday from start-ups alone.
2. **Dilution.** With the rules at about a fifth of the file, they sit among pages of tables and procedure, and the ones that matter get lost. A data generation agent doesn't need the μP width axis, and a sweep agent doesn't need the b-beam mass.

**The correction.** CLAUDE.md holds three things, not two:
1. **The rules,** as agreed.
2. **A short orientation,** always fed: what the project is, its research threads and the main entry points. A few hundred tokens.
3. **An index of the sections,** always fed: one line each, saying what the section covers and what triggers it. An agent then knows the reference exists, and can read a section on purpose when its work needs it before any trigger fires.

This goes into the redraft with the regrouping and the stay-or-go test. The mapping will then show three possible destinations for each passage: rule, orientation or section.
